Modal Verbs Review: Can, Have To, Should, Must, Could
Modal verbs are auxiliary verbs that cannot work as the main verb in a sentence. They are used to express possibility, obligation, advisability, request, necessity and ability.
You can keep doing business the way you usually do or you could try to improve by using the new business productivity applications that run on mobile-device-based or web-based technologies.
Companies that want to keep up with changes, must adapt to new technologies.
We know for a fact that these technology trends are becoming more relevant and anyone who wants to take advantage of their benefits, has to stay up to date with them.
We can use modal verbs to give advice, recommendation and suggestions to someone. The most common modal verbs we use for this purpose are:

Examples:
To speed up the process of internal verbal communication, you should try to implement mobile-based technologies.
If you are really interested in saving money, you must make use of cloud computing services in your company.
We can use modal verbs to express certainty and uncertainty. Depending on how certain we feel about someone or something, we may use any of the modal verbs outlined below:

Example:
Samantha sent me a text message. She says she could try to attend the meeting today. On the other hand, Charles phoned me. He said he has too much office work. However, he might attend the meeting if he's able to finish by tomorrow.
We can use modal verbs to express obligation or that something is mandatory. For this, we can use the following modal verbs:

Example:
The IT department implemented a security protocol for all the company's employees. We have to enter a double password to get access to our email account.
Finally, we can use the verb can to express that someone has the ability to do something.

Example:
I can make companies save money by streamlining processes thanks to the use of information technologies. I'm really savvy on it.
We can use the verbs will and might to refer to future actions or events.

Depending on how certain we feel about a future situation or how sure we are that something is going to take place, we may choose between the verbs will and might. Will expresses a much stronger certainty and we use it to talk about plans or established events in the future.
It is evident that we will see in the near future companies that will provide employees with sophisticated smartphones to synchronize tasks, calendars, an entire projects via these machines.

We might see doctors checking up patients online and getting all the information they need like the patient's record by keeping their mobiles synched with those of their colleagues, nurses, vendors from pharmaceutical labs and administrative staff.

Examples:
Tomorrow, we will restructure the code and hire new employees to finish the project.
We will go over all the requirements for information management systems in next week's meeting.
On the other hand, when we want to express that we are not entirely sure about a future event, we can use the verb might.

Examples:
We might be able to improve the processes in the company if we assess the metrics we are using.
I'm not entirely sure, but we might have a meeting tomorrow morning.

images.text: You can keep doing business the way you usually do or you could try to improve by using the new business productivity applications that run on mobile-device-based or web-based technologies. The era of paper-based letters, memos, circulars and other documents alike is a matter of the past. Companies that want to keep up with changes, must adapt to new technologies. Computers and specially software applications gradually transform the way companies should do business and manage their operations. Just imagine how email messaging and videoconferencing are now the new standard form of documents and the most practical form of communication. We can now send hundreds of emails and talk to people located everywhere in the world in real time, making businesses save millions of dollars a year.

But that's not all. Technology keeps evolving and more productivity applications are emerging. Handheld devices like smartphones and tablets are becoming an important driving force for communications and business operations. We cannot forget the tremendous impact that cloud computing and collaborative work are creating on the way businesses work.  We know for a fact that these technology trends are becoming more relevant and anyone who wants to take advantage of their benefits, has to stay up to date with them.  Not only start-ups but also large firms are investing heavily in these technologies. It is evident that we will see in the near future companies that will provide employees with sophisticated smartphones to synchronize tasks, calendars and entire projects, all via these devices and the use of specialized applications.

For example, we might see doctors checking up patients online and getting all the information they need like the patient's record by keeping their mobiles synched with those of their colleagues, nurses, vendors from pharmaceutical labs and administrative staff.  Sales representatives, for instance, might get in touch with their clients and monitor their needs via telephone messaging apps. Besides, due to cloud information storage on the web, it wouldn't matter if you lived in Canada, China or Chile as videoconferencing and collaborative work will be easier than ever.
